text:
Jules: Quick announcement — we pushed the new 'slice-packer' microbatcher to a 10% canary on hosted-prod 20m ago. Early telemetry looks strong: p50 down ~33%, p99 down ~33%, and unit token cost ~10% lower. More details below. :tada:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: service=inference-runtime, image=rbw/runtime:v2.9-slice-packer, rollout=10% (triggered by @Jules)

Alex: Nice. Which model and traffic slice did you test on?

Jules: Baseline test = steady-chat-medium traffic (real production mix). Model: redwood-gpt-small-2026. Analysis window: first 30m after ramp. Numbers vs baseline (same 30m window):
- p50: 48ms -> 32ms (~33% improvement)
- p95: 180ms -> 120ms (~33% improvement)
- p99: 420ms -> 280ms (~33% improvement)
- Tokens/unit cost: ~10% decrease from smarter packing + reduced per-token kernel overhead
- GPU memory overhead: +~2% at 10% rollout
- Throughput: effective requests/sec up ~8% (better packing utilization)
Link: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/slice-packer-canary (perf/trace samples)

Marta: Good numbers. Any regressions for short requests (<64 tokens) or safety signals (error rate, timeouts)?

Jules: Short requests are essentially flat — slice-packer mainly helps mid-length workloads (128–512 tokens). No increase in error rate, connection resets, or tail timeouts observed in the canary window. QA harness ran lightweight prompt-sanity and production evals (passes).

Ryan: What are the ops knobs if we need to roll back quickly?

Jules: Rollout command we used:```bash
./ops/rollout --service inference-runtime --feature slice_packer=on --pct 10
```
Rollback:```bash
./ops/rollback --service inference-runtime --feature slice_packer
```
We also set an automatic rollback rule: if p99 increases by >10% for 5m or error-rate +0.5% over baseline for 5m -> abort.

Cory: Kernel/quantization compatibility? Any model types where this hurts perf?

Jules: Tested on INT8 quantized kernels and fp16 paths across Ampere and Hopper nodes. Compatible. One edge: seq>2048 fallback currently takes ~0.5% extra time due to packing alignment — tracked in issue RBW-487. No functional regressions.

Alex: Any plans to expand to Dedicated/private fleets? timeline?

Jules: Next steps: extend canary to 30% tomorrow morning (after 24h sanity on 10%), run 24h long-tail soak, bake into the release notes, and stage rollout to Dedicated next week (with perf gates). I'll open the RFC and follow-up doc for the tuning knobs.

Marta: :rocket: Thanks for the quick work. Please ping infra on the long-tail soak so we can reserve capacity.

Jules: Will do. Tagging follow-ups: /assign @Ryan to monitor rollback alerts, @Cory to validate multi-GPU scaling, and I'll file the postmortem-style notes in docs once the 30% canary finishes.

deploy-bot: Canary health checks ok (30m) — latency, errors, cpu/gpu metrics within thresholds.

Jules: TL;DR: slice-packer = ~33% latency win across mid-tail, ~10% cost reduction, canary healthy, expanding cautiously.
